cards.name: Ground friction, acceleration and speed caps
cards.summary: Walking loses 6 times the larger of speed and 100 per second to friction, gains 10 times the wish speed per second of acceleration, and is capped at 300 units per second (100 while crouched).
cards.behavior: The movement step runs once per input command. Its time step is the command length in milliseconds times 0.001. Friction runs first. The speed drop equals the larger of the current speed and the stop speed 100, times the friction value 6, times the time step. Friction applies only on solid ground that is not marked slippery, or on a ladder. Below 1 unit per second the horizontal velocity is set to zero. Acceleration then compares the speed along the wished direction with the wished speed. It adds at most the shortfall. One step adds at most acceleration 10 times the time step times the wished speed. The wished speed is capped at 300, or at 100 while crouched. The keyboard sends 200 per axis by default and doubles that when run is on, so the 300 cap sets the real run speed. Ground and air movement build the wish vector from the view angles with the pitch divided by 3. Looking steeply up or down costs only a little forward speed. These numbers are file-level defaults in the shared movement code. This source tree has no other assignment to them.

constants.unit: units per second; floor on the speed used to scale friction, per command step

constants.unit: dimensionless factor; speed lost per second equals factor times the larger of speed and stop speed, per command step

constants.unit: dimensionless factor; speed gained per second equals factor times wish speed, per command step

constants.unit: units per second while the crouch flag is set

constants.unit: units per second per axis before the run doubling

constants.name: friction cutoff speed
constants.unit: units per second; below it horizontal velocity is zeroed

constants.name: command time scale

cards.name: Air control in single player and the optional strafe mode
cards.summary: With the default air acceleration of 0 the air step reuses the ground formula at acceleration 1, which is one tenth of ground control and has no 30 unit strafe cap.
cards.behavior: The air acceleration setting defaults to 0 on the server. Single player forces it to 0 through the configuration string. Only deathmatch passes the server setting on. When the setting is 0, the airborne step calls the ordinary acceleration function with an acceleration of 1. That adds at most 1 times the wish speed times the time step, so 300 units per second squared at full input, against 3000 on the ground. There is no friction in the air. When a server sets a nonzero air acceleration, a second function runs instead. It clamps the wished speed to 30 for the add-speed test but scales each push by the full wished speed and the ground acceleration value 10. That second mode is what allows strafe turning. Gravity is subtracted after acceleration, once per command, as gravity times the time step. Treat the 0 default as the single player feel: a jump commits to its direction and only bends slowly. Add the clamped mode only when a deathmatch style feel is wanted.

constants.name: air acceleration default
constants.unit: units per second squared selector; 0 selects the weak air path

constants.name: server air acceleration default
constants.unit: cvar default; applies in deathmatch only

constants.name: single player forced air acceleration
constants.unit: value written to the shared setting when deathmatch is off

constants.name: air fallback acceleration
constants.unit: dimensionless factor; speed gained per second equals factor times wish speed, per command step

constants.name: strafe mode wish speed clamp
constants.unit: units per second used only in the add-speed test when the setting is nonzero

constants.name: gravity
constants.unit: units per second squared; server default, a map can override it

capabilities: optional capped air acceleration for strafe turning

cards.name: Jump impulse and hard-landing jump lockout
cards.summary: A jump sets vertical speed to at least 270 units per second (about 45 units of rise under gravity 800), needs the button released between jumps, and a hard landing blocks jumping for 144 or 200 ms.
cards.behavior: A jump needs a vertical command of at least 10, a floor under the player and a live player. The jump-held flag blocks a second jump until the command drops below 10. A jump adds 270 to the vertical velocity and raises it to 270 when it is lower. The step then applies gravity once per command. Rise is about 270 squared over twice gravity, which is near 45 units. Rise varies a little with command length because gravity is stepped, not solved exactly. Landing sets a timer in units of 8 ms. A landing faster than 200 units per second down sets 18 units (144 ms). Faster than 400 sets 25 units (200 ms). While the timer runs the player cannot jump. The timer ticks down by the command length shifted right by 3 bits. In water the same button swims instead of jumping. The server also plays a jump sound and posts a noise when the player leaves the floor with the button held.

constants.name: jump impulse
constants.unit: units per second upward added at launch; floor on resulting vertical speed

constants.name: jump command threshold
constants.unit: upward command value needed to count as jump held

constants.name: hard landing speed
constants.unit: units per second; vertical speed below this gives the long lockout

constants.name: hard landing lockout
constants.unit: timer units of 8 ms each (200 ms)

constants.name: soft landing speed
constants.unit: units per second; vertical speed below this gives the short lockout

constants.name: soft landing lockout
constants.unit: timer units of 8 ms each (144 ms)

constants.name: timer shift
constants.unit: right shift applied to command milliseconds, so the timer counts in 8 ms units

capabilities: fixed impulse jump with gravity stepped per command
landing recovery after a long fall

cards.name: Slide collision, stair stepping and ground contact
cards.summary: Movement slides along up to 5 planes in 4 bumps, retries blocked moves lifted by 18 units and keeps the farther result, and counts as grounded when a 0.25 unit probe hits a surface with normal at least 0.7.
cards.behavior: The slide routine traces the remaining time along the velocity, up to 4 times. After each hit it clips the velocity against every stored plane with an overbounce of 1.01 and tiny components under 0.1 become zero. If clipping leaves no valid direction and there are exactly two planes, it slides along their crease. With other plane counts it stops. If the new velocity opposes the original, it stops dead to avoid corner jitter. The stair routine runs the slide once from the start. It then lifts the start by 18 units, slides again with the original velocity, and presses down by 18. It keeps the lifted result when it travelled farther in the horizontal plane and the landing normal is at least 0.7. Otherwise it keeps the flat result. Ground contact traces 0.25 units down from the origin. It fails when the player rises faster than 180 units per second or the surface normal is below 0.7. Positions and velocities are stored in 16-bit integers at one eighth unit precision.

constants.unit: units lifted and pressed back during the stair retry

constants.name: minimum step landing normal
constants.unit: vertical component of the surface normal

constants.name: slide overbounce
constants.unit: dimensionless clip factor applied to the velocity into each plane

constants.name: tiny velocity cutoff
constants.unit: units per second; clipped components below this become zero

constants.name: walkable floor normal
constants.unit: vertical component of the floor normal

constants.name: rising speed that drops ground contact

capabilities: climb stairs and curbs at full speed

cards.name: Crouch as an instant hull swap
cards.summary: The player hull is 32 units wide by 56 tall (half-width 16, from -24 to 32), and crouch instantly shrinks the top to 4 (28 tall) and the eye height from 22 to -2, with a ceiling check to stand.
cards.behavior: Each command first rebuilds the hull. The horizontal half-extent is 16 on both axes, so the box is 32 units wide. The bottom is 24 below the origin. Standing, the top is 32 above the origin, giving 56 units of height, and the eye sits 22 above the origin. Crouch needs a downward vertical command while on the ground. It sets the flag at once with no timed transition. The top drops to 4, giving 28 units of height, and the eye height becomes -2. The speed cap for ground and air drops to 100. While crouched without the key, the code tests the standing hull at the current origin and clears the flag only when that box is free of solid. Leaving the ground also tries to stand, even with the key held. A dead player is forced into the crouched hull. A gibbed player uses a small hull from 0 to 16 with the eye at 8.

constants.name: hull half-width
constants.unit: units on X and Y; full width is 32

constants.name: standing hull top
constants.unit: units relative to the origin; full height 56

constants.name: crouched hull top
constants.unit: units relative to the origin; full height 28

capabilities: instant crouch with no camera ease

cards.name: Swimming, sinking, jump in water and currents
cards.summary: At waist depth the player swims in 3D at half of the 300 cap (150), sinks at 60 units per second with no input, and water currents add up to 400 units per second to the wish vector.
cards.behavior: Water depth has three levels from sample points at the feet, the mid body and the eye. Level 2 or higher switches to the swim step. The wish vector follows the full view direction, pitch included, plus the up command. With no input at all the player drifts down at 60. The result is capped at 300 and then halved, so the swim cap is 150 units per second. Water acceleration is 10 and uses the ordinary acceleration function. Drag removes speed in proportion to the speed, the water friction 1 and the depth level, so deeper water slows more. Gravity does not run while swimming. Pressing jump at level 2 or higher sets upward speed to 100 in water, 80 in slime or 50 in lava, unless the player already falls faster than 300. Currents flagged in the water volume add a push of 400 along the flagged direction. At level 1 on the ground the push is halved. Conveyor floors add a fixed 100 push.

constants.unit: depth level at or above which the swim step runs

constants.name: idle sink speed
constants.unit: units per second downward added when no input is held

constants.name: swim speed scale

constants.name: water acceleration

constants.name: water friction
constants.unit: dimensionless factor times depth level times speed, per command step

constants.name: water current speed
constants.unit: units per second added along the flagged direction

constants.name: fast sink limit for swim jump
constants.unit: units per second; falling faster blocks the swim jump

constants.name: conveyor push

cards.name: Ladders by look pitch and the water ledge hop
cards.summary: A flagged ladder volume ahead lets look pitch beyond 15 degrees with forward input climb or descend at 200 units per second, and a chest-deep player facing a ledge hops out with 350 up and 50 forward for up to 255 timer units.
cards.behavior: Each command traces 1 unit ahead on the horizontal. If the hit surface carries the ladder flag the ladder state is on. On a ladder, ground friction still applies, gravity does not, and the wish vector is edited. Forward input with the view pitched up by 15 degrees or more sets the vertical wish to 200. Pitched down by 15 or more it sets -200. Without pitch, the up and down commands set 200 or -200. Otherwise the vertical wish is 0 and the vertical velocity bleeds toward zero by gravity. Horizontal wish is clamped to 25 on each axis. The edit applies only while the vertical speed magnitude is 200 or less. The ledge hop needs water depth level 2 and no active timer. It probes 30 units ahead and 4 up for solid. It then probes 16 higher for empty space. When both pass, it sets 50 units per second forward and 350 up, and starts a timer of 255 units. Gravity applies during the hop, steering is off, and the timer clears when the vertical speed turns negative.

constants.unit: degrees; at or below it forward input climbs

constants.name: look-down pitch threshold
constants.unit: degrees; at or above it forward input descends

constants.name: ladder edit vertical speed limit
constants.unit: units per second; edits apply only up to this magnitude

constants.name: ledge clearance rise
constants.unit: additional units above the low probe

constants.name: ledge hop forward speed
constants.unit: units per second along the facing

constants.name: ledge hop timer
constants.unit: timer units of 8 ms (2040 ms upper bound; ends early when falling)

capabilities: stopping dead on a ladder when idle

cards.name: Command timing, client prediction and one eighth unit positions
cards.summary: The same movement step runs per input command on both sides, the client replays unacknowledged commands, snaps when it misses by more than 80 units, and smooths stair steps over 100 ms against a 10 Hz server.
cards.behavior: Each client frame becomes one command whose length is the frame time in milliseconds. A command longer than 250 ms is replaced by 100 ms. The input module also limits one frame to 200 ms. The server runs the identical movement function for each received command. The server world ticks at 10 Hz, with the time advanced by 100 ms per frame. The client keeps the commands the server has not acknowledged. Each frame it starts from the last server player state and replays them, which yields the predicted origin. When a new server state arrives, it compares the server origin with the stored prediction for the acknowledged command. When the summed integer error exceeds 640 (80 units) it clears the error as a teleport. Otherwise it stores the error and the view applies it. Positions are stored as 16-bit integers at one eighth unit. After a move the origin is rounded and tested against the world. Eight neighbour roundings are tried and the previous position is used when none is valid. When a replayed command raises the origin by 7.9 to 20 units on the ground, the view subtracts the step and fades it out over 100 ms.

constants.name: overlong frame replaced
constants.unit: milliseconds; a longer frame time is treated as unreasonable

constants.name: error scale
constants.unit: world units per stored integer unit

constants.name: step smoothing time
constants.unit: milliseconds to fade the stair offset

constants.name: velocity storage scale
constants.unit: stored integer units per world unit per second

capabilities: snap on large misses and smooth correction on small ones

cards.name: Fall damage from squared speed change
cards.summary: Fall strength is the squared vertical speed change times 0.0001, so damage starts near 548 units per second and equals (strength - 30) / 2, with armor still absorbing it.
cards.behavior: At the end of each server frame the code compares the vertical speed with the previous frame. A player standing on the floor uses the vertical speed change since the last frame. A player still in the air who was suddenly slowed uses the old downward speed. Strength is that change squared times 0.0001. Fully submerged players take nothing. Waist-deep strength is multiplied by 0.25 and level 1 by 0.5. Below 1 nothing happens. Below 15 only a footstep event plays. From 15 the view dips for 0.3 seconds by half the strength, up to 40. Strength above 30 deals damage of (strength - 30) divided by 2, at least 1. Strength of 55 or more selects the louder fall sound. Strength 30 matches about 548 units per second, 55 about 742. A fall at 800 units per second deals about 17 and at 1000 about 35. The damage call passes no flags, so armor absorbs it. Deathmatch can turn fall damage off by flag.

constants.name: strength scale
constants.unit: per unit squared of vertical speed change per server frame (10 Hz)

constants.name: waist-deep scale
constants.unit: multiplier on strength at water depth level 2

constants.name: shin-deep scale
constants.unit: multiplier on strength at water depth level 1

constants.name: footstep ceiling
constants.unit: strength units; below this only a footstep plays

constants.name: damage threshold
constants.unit: strength units; damage starts above it

constants.name: loud fall strength
constants.unit: strength units for the louder fall event

constants.name: view dip scale
constants.unit: view dip amount per strength unit

cards.name: Head bob, run lean and weapon sway
cards.summary: View bob advances 0.25, 0.125 or 0.0625 per server frame by speed band, adds up to 6 units of vertical bob and small pitch and roll scaled by horizontal speed, plus gun sway and a clamped view offset.
cards.behavior: The bob clock advances each 0.1 second server frame. The step is chosen on the ground only: 0.25 above 210 units per second, 0.125 above 100 and 0.0625 otherwise. In the air the last step keeps running. The clock resets below 5. The clock is multiplied by 4 while crouched. The bob wave is the absolute value of a sine of the clock times pi. The integer part of the clock gives a cycle number that flips the roll sign and times footstep sounds when speed passes 225. Vertical bob is the wave times speed times 0.005, capped at 6 units. View pitch bob uses 0.002 per unit of speed and roll bob 0.002, both times 6 when crouched. Run lean adds 0.002 times the forward speed to pitch and 0.005 times the sideways speed to roll. The gun model sways with roll 0.005 and yaw 0.01 per unit of speed times the wave, plus a lag of 0.2 of the recent view angle change limited to 45 degrees. The final view offset is clamped to 14 units on each horizontal axis and from -22 to 30 vertically.

constants.unit: clock units per server frame (10 Hz) above 210 units per second

constants.name: medium bob step

cards.name: Damage view kick and screen tint
cards.summary: Each hit kicks the view by up to 50 scaled by 0.3 over 0.5 seconds and raises a red tint of 0.2 to 0.6 alpha that fades 0.06 per 0.1 second server frame.
cards.behavior: All damage taken in one server frame is summed into blood, armor and power armor parts. Totals below 10 count as 10 so a hit always shows. The tint alpha grows by 0.01 per point, with a floor of 0.2 and a cap of 0.6, and its color mixes red for blood, white for armor and green for power armor by share. It fades by 0.06 each server frame. The kick starts from the knockback, scaled by 100 over current health, raised to half the total and capped at 50. The roll equals kick times the sideways share of the hit direction times 0.3. The pitch uses the forward share the same way. The kick fades linearly over 0.5 seconds. A pain sound plays at most once per 0.7 seconds and its tier follows health under 25, 50 and 75. Water, lava and slime add a screen tint with alpha 0.4 for water and 0.6 for lava or being inside a wall. On the easiest skill the player takes half damage.

constants.name: alpha fade
constants.unit: tint alpha per server frame (10 Hz)

constants.name: kick health scale
constants.unit: knockback times this divided by current health

constants.name: easy skill damage scale
constants.unit: multiplier on damage to the player

capabilities: tint that mixes blood, armor and power armor
minimum visible feedback for small hits

cards.name: Armor tiers and power armor
cards.summary: Three armor tiers absorb 30, 60 or 80 percent of normal damage (0, 30 or 60 percent of energy damage) and spend one armor point per absorbed point, after power armor absorbs two thirds or a third from cells.
cards.behavior: Damage passes through three stages. First, invulnerability or god mode can zero it. Second, power armor takes its share and spends cells. Third, worn armor takes a share and loses the same number of points. Worn armor absorbs the protection fraction times the damage, rounded up, but never more than the armor still held. The jacket tier grants 25 when picked up bare and holds up to 50, with 30 percent normal and 0 percent energy protection. The combat tier grants 50, holds 100, with 60 and 30 percent. The body tier grants 100, holds 200, with 80 and 60 percent. Power armor comes in two kinds. The screen kind works only for hits from the front, where the hit direction has a dot product above 0.3 with the facing. It absorbs one third of the damage at 1 point per cell. The shield kind works from all sides, absorbs two thirds and spends 1 cell per 2 points. Drowning bypasses all armor. Falls and liquids do not.

constants.unit: armor points granted when no armor is held

constants.name: combat pickup armor
constants.unit: armor points granted when no armor is held

constants.name: body pickup armor
constants.unit: armor points granted when no armor is held

constants.unit: damage divided by this is absorbed

cards.name: Splash falloff, knockback and self launch
cards.summary: Splash damage equals the base minus half the distance to the target box center, halved again for the shooter, and knockback pushes 500 times the knockback over mass, rising to 1600 for self hits.
cards.behavior: Splash finds every damageable entity in the radius. Distance runs from the explosion to the center of the target box. Points equal the base damage minus half that distance. The shooter gets half of the points. A target takes damage only when the explosion has a clear line to its origin or to one of four corners offset by 15 units on both axes. Moving brush models use their center instead. The points are also the knockback. The velocity change is the hit direction times 500 times the knockback divided by the target mass. The mass floor is 50. Player mass is 200. When a player hurts themself, the 500 becomes 1600, which enables launch jumps. A rocket with radius 120 and base 120 still deals 60 at the radius edge, then 0 outside. On a monster that has no enemy yet, a direct hit by a player deals double damage.

constants.unit: damage points lost per unit of distance

constants.name: self splash scale

constants.name: knockback scale
constants.unit: velocity units per unit of knockback per unit of mass (applied once per hit)

constants.name: self knockback scale
constants.unit: same formula when a player hurts themself

constants.name: surprise multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier on a monster with no enemy

capabilities: linear splash falloff with a hard edge

cards.name: Rockets, launcher grenades and hand grenades
cards.summary: Rockets fly straight at 650 units per second for 100 to 119 direct and 120 splash, launcher grenades bounce at 600 for a 2.5 second fuse, and hand grenades throw 400 to 800 on a 3 second fuse.
cards.behavior: A rocket spawns near the view. It flies without gravity at 650 units per second and lives 8000 divided by its speed in seconds. On touching a damageable body it deals 100 plus a random 0 to 19 as a direct hit, then splash of 120 within radius 120 that skips the body already hit. Walls only splash. A launcher grenade has damage 120 and a radius of damage plus 40. It leaves at 600, with extra upward speed of 200 and sideways jitter of 10. It spins at 300 degrees per second on each axis. It bounces with an overbounce of 1.5. It rests on a floor with normal above 0.7 once its vertical speed is under 60. It explodes on its 2.5 second timer, or on touching a damageable entity. Touching walls only plays a bounce sound. A hand grenade is thrown at 400 plus extra speed up to 800 depending on how long the button was held. The fuse is 3 seconds plus a 0.2 second grace, and it counts down while the button is held. A hand grenade held too long explodes in the hand. The next throw waits 1 second. The server ticks projectiles every 0.1 second.

cards.name: Weapon cadence from 10 Hz animation frames
cards.summary: Each weapon steps one animation frame per 0.1 second server tick, so rates are tick counts: machine gun 10 shots per second, chain gun 10, 20 then 30, hyperblaster 10, and slower weapons repeat every 0.5 to 2.5 seconds (derived).
cards.behavior: The weapon logic is a frame state machine with ready, firing, activating and dropping states. It runs once per 0.1 second server frame. Extra input commands within the same frame do not step it again. Firing sets the first fire frame, calls the fire function on the listed fire frames and advances one frame per tick. The weapon returns to ready when the frame passes the end of the fire range. With the button held it refires on the next tick. Rates below are counted from the frame tables and may be off by one tick. Blaster about 0.5 seconds, rocket launcher 0.9, shotgun 1.2, double barrel shotgun 1.2, grenade launcher 1.2, rail gun 1.6, heavy energy sphere weapon 2.5 counted from one shot to the next, including its pre-fire frames. The machine gun alternates two frames and fires on each, so 10 per second. The chain gun fires 1 shot per tick up to frame 9, 2 per tick up to frame 14 while held, then 3 per tick, so 10, 20, then 30 shots per second. The hyperblaster fires once per tick. Idle fidget frames are skipped 15 times out of 16. Weapon switching plays a lowering animation and then raises the new one.

constants.name: server tick
constants.unit: seconds per weapon state machine step

constants.name: chain gun single shot frame limit
chain gun double shot frame limit
idle fidget skip mask
constants.unit: random mask; the fidget is skipped unless the masked roll is 0

cards.name: Bullet and pellet spread, climb and per-weapon damage
cards.summary: Rays aim at a point 8192 units out with a uniform offset of up to 300 by 500 (bullets) or 1000 by 500 (pellets), the machine gun climbs 1.5 degrees per shot up to 9 shots, and water doubles the spread.
cards.behavior: Each bullet or pellet picks a uniform random sideways offset and a uniform random vertical offset at a far point 8192 units along the aim. The bullet limits are 300 and 500. The pellet limits are 1000 and 500. The result is a rectangle, not a bell curve. A ray that crosses water is re-aimed from the water surface with the offsets doubled. The shotgun fires 12 pellets of 4 damage and kick 8. The double barrel fires 20 pellets of 6 damage and kick 12 as two groups of 10, each aimed 5 degrees to one side of the view. The machine gun fires 1 bullet of 8 damage and kick 2 per tick. In single player the machine gun adds 1.5 degrees of upward aim per sustained shot, counting up to 9 shots, so the spray climbs. The chain gun also jitters the muzzle position and deals 8 damage, or 6 in deathmatch. Each shot also adds a small random view kick that is cleared at the end of the frame. Impacts on the world post a noise that monsters can hear.

cards.name: Rail gun piercing hitscan
cards.summary: The rail gun traces 8192 units with no spread, deals 150 (100 in deathmatch) to each monster or player along the line, and stops only at world geometry.
cards.behavior: The shot is an instant straight trace from the muzzle. It never misses by spread. The trace loops. At each hit on a monster or a player it applies damage and then continues from that point while ignoring that body. It stops at the first thing that is not a monster or player. Slime and lava surfaces are crossed once and flagged so the beam draws on both sides. The weapon deals 150 damage with kick 250 in single player and 100 with kick 200 in deathmatch. The kick is the knockback applied to a hit target. The shooter view gets a 3 unit back push and 3 degrees of upward kick. Fire happens on frame 4, and the full cycle is about 1.6 seconds (derived). A hit posts an impact noise at the end point. Rail shots skip the projectile dodge warning, so monsters get no chance to duck them.
capabilities: instant pierce through all living targets

cards.name: Heavy energy sphere with tether lasers and sqrt falloff
cards.summary: The sphere flies at 400 units per second, zaps every living target within 256 units for 10 per 0.1 second tick, then bursts at 200 direct plus a radius 1000 blast with square-root falloff.
cards.behavior: The weapon has a pre-fire frame at 9 and the shot at frame 17. The sphere travels without gravity at 400 units per second for up to 8000 divided by speed seconds, which is 20 seconds. While it flies, every 0.1 second tick it looks for monsters, players and explosive barrels within 256 units. For each one it traces a line up to 2048 units in that direction and damages everything along it that takes damage and is not immune, at 10 per tick in single player and 5 in deathmatch. On impact it deals 200 to the body hit and 200 splash in radius 100 elsewhere. After one tick the blast fires once at frame 0 of a five frame animation (0.5 seconds). It hits every target within 1000 units that is visible from both the blast and the owner, except the owner. Damage is the base (500 in single player, 200 in deathmatch) times one minus the square root of the distance over the radius. Half the radius still gives about 29 percent.

cards.name: Powerup timers in server frames
cards.summary: Timed powerups last 300 server frames (30 seconds at 10 Hz), flicker in the last 30 frames, the damage boost multiplies damage and kick by 4, and the silencer lasts 30 shots.
cards.behavior: Powerups store an end frame number. Use adds 300 frames to the current frame, or adds to the remaining time when already active. At 10 frames per second that is 30 seconds. With the damage boost active, each weapon multiplies its damage and its kick by 4. Invulnerability sets all damage taken to zero except flagged no-protection damage. It plays a sound at most every 2 seconds on a hit. The rebreather and the environment suit also last 300 frames and refill the air timer to 10 seconds while under water. In the last 30 frames, the powerup effect and the screen tint show only when bit 4 of the remaining frame count is set, so they flicker. A warning sound plays when exactly 30 frames remain. The silencer counts 30 shots, and each weapon noise consumes one shot and is not posted to monsters.

constants.name: flicker bit
constants.unit: bit mask on the remaining frame count

capabilities: silenced shots that stay hidden from monsters

cards.name: Monster sight cone, range bands and noise hearing
cards.summary: Monsters check one player per frame, see in a cone of dot above 0.3 inside range bands of 80, 500 and 1000 units, ignore a player in near darkness, and hear noise posted within the last frame out to 1000 units.
cards.behavior: Each server frame one living player is picked as the sight target. Ranges are bands by distance: melee under 80, near under 500, mid under 1000 and far beyond. A far player is never noticed by sight. The monster needs an unblocked eye-to-eye line, and the player light level must exceed 5. At near range the target must lie in front, because only monsters ever set the wake flag in this source, never the player. At mid range the player must lie in front. Front means the dot product of the facing and the direction to the target is above 0.3, a cone with about a 145 degree total spread. A monster that notices a player marks itself hostile for 1 second. Monsters that see an alerted neighbour join it, which is why the alerting monster gets light level 128. Hearing uses noise entities. The player posts a noise when firing without a silencer, when bullets hit the world, when jumping and when entering or leaving water. A noise counts only in the frame it is posted and the next frame. The monster must be within the sound area, within 1000 units and in a connected area. It then turns toward the noise. Ambush monsters react to a noise only when they can see its source. Deathmatch posts no noise.

constants.name: front dot threshold
constants.unit: dot product of facing and direction to target

constants.name: minimum light level
constants.unit: light level units; at or below it the player is unseen

constants.name: noise freshness
constants.unit: server frames (10 Hz) after the frame it was posted

constants.name: light level after being spotted
constants.unit: light level units set on the monster that found the player

capabilities: dark corners that hide the player
noise that pulls monsters toward a spot
one sight check per frame to save time

cards.name: Per-tick attack chance by range band
cards.summary: Each 0.1 second tick a monster with a clear shot starts a missile attack with chance 0.1 near and 0.02 mid (0.4 when holding ground), scaled by difficulty, then waits up to 2 seconds. Melee range always attacks.
cards.behavior: The attack check runs while the enemy is visible. A trace from eye to eye must hit the enemy first, so another monster in the way blocks the shot. At melee range the monster attacks at once, using melee if it has one. On the easiest skill 3 of 4 melee checks are skipped. Otherwise the monster needs an attack move, a finished cooldown and a non-far range. The chance per tick is 0.4 for a monster told to hold its ground, 0.1 near and 0.02 mid. A third chance value of 0.2 for melee range sits in the code but cannot run, because melee range returns earlier. The easiest skill halves the chance and skills 2 and 3 double it. A passed roll starts the attack and sets a cooldown of 0 to 2 seconds. When a monster first starts hunting, it waits 1 second before the first attack. Flying monsters that fail the roll pick sliding sideways with chance 0.3 or flying straight. The monster turns in place until it faces within 45 degrees of the target before the attack starts. A dead enemy ends the fight, and a monster flagged brutal keeps attacking corpses until their health reaches -80.

constants.name: attack cooldown range
constants.unit: seconds; cooldown is a random value up to this

constants.name: easy melee skip mask
constants.unit: random mask; a nonzero masked roll skips the melee attack

constants.name: facing tolerance
constants.unit: degrees; larger error blocks the attack

constants.name: brutal corpse health limit
constants.unit: health at or below which a brutal monster stops

capabilities: friendly fire blocking by monsters in the line

cards.name: Pursuit by last sighting and the player breadcrumb trail
cards.summary: A monster that loses sight heads for the last seen point, probes 16 units to each side when a wall blocks it, and then follows a ring of 8 breadcrumbs the player left.
cards.behavior: While the enemy is visible the monster walks straight at it and records the position and time. On losing sight it flags lost sight and targets the last seen point. If a trace to that point is blocked, it traces two side probes 16 units to each side at a point partway there. It picks the clearer side and sets a temporary goal. On reaching the point it asks the trail for the next marker. The trail is a ring of 8 positions. In single player the player adds a position each frame while not visible from the latest marker, which gives sparse breadcrumbs around corners. The monster picks the first marker newer than the last one it used, and steps along them. The search timer is 5 seconds from the last sighting. A sound target expires 5 seconds after the noise. A monster that reaches within 64 units of a noise target stops and holds position. Deathmatch has no trail.

constants.name: side probe offset
constants.unit: units to the left of the line to the goal; the right probe uses +16

constants.name: extended search timeout
constants.unit: seconds added to the search timer before it resets

constants.name: noise stop distance
constants.unit: units from the noise target to hold position

capabilities: chase to the last seen spot

cards.name: Monster stepping, edge checks and turning
cards.summary: Monsters move by animation frames at 10 Hz, step up 18 units, refuse unsupported edges, turn at most 20 degrees per tick for walkers (10 for flyers) and must face within 45 degrees of a move.
cards.behavior: The monster brain thinks every 0.1 second. Each tick advances one animation frame, and the frame table gives a distance for that frame, scaled by the model scale. Motion is the move function that tries a step: it lifts by 18 units, traces down twice that, and refuses steps into water for walkers. After the move the bottom check requires solid under all four corners, or under the middle with no corner drop above 18 units. Otherwise the move is undone. Turning is limited each tick by the monster turn speed. Walkers default to 20 degrees and flyers to 10, and a monster type can set its own. A step is cancelled when the monster still faces more than 45 degrees from the direction. Direction choice favors the straight line to the goal, changes by multiples of 45 degrees, never turns back directly and re-rolls by chance 1 in 4 each tick. Flyers and swimmers change height by 8 units per step toward the goal. Walkers and flyers use an eye height of 25 units. Water depth uses a probe 26 units above the first one, then another 22 units higher.

constants.name: reroll mask
constants.unit: random mask; a roll of 1 triggers a new direction (1 in 4 per tick)

constants.name: bottom check depth factor
constants.unit: multiples of the step height traced downward

constants.name: flyer height step
constants.unit: units per move toward the goal height

cards.name: Pain gating, dodging and infighting
cards.summary: A soldier flinches at most once per 3 seconds (never on the hardest skill), dodges incoming projectiles with chance 0.25, and monsters that hit each other turn on the attacker.
cards.behavior: The pain handler returns early when called within 3 seconds of the last pain. In that window it only upgrades an airborne flinch. Its skin changes when health falls under half. The hardest skill plays no flinch animation. The damage routine also locks pain for 5 seconds on that skill. Otherwise a random roll picks one of three flinch moves, thirds at 0.33 and 0.66. A launched monster with upward speed over 100 plays its own flinch. Projectile firing checks a line out to 8192 units for a monster ahead of it and gives that monster the time to impact. The monster then rolls 0.25 and may duck or fire back. Easier skills duck more often. The check itself runs at 25 percent on the easiest skill. Infighting: a monster hit by another monster of the same movement class takes the attacker as its new enemy, unless the attacker is one of the heavy bosses or tanks, which spray too widely. Friendly flagged monsters never retaliate against players.

constants.name: skin change fraction divisor
constants.unit: health under max health divided by this changes the skin

constants.name: dodge hold extra
constants.unit: seconds added to the projectile arrival time

constants.name: easy skill warning chance
constants.unit: probability that the warning runs at all

capabilities: projectile dodging with a time window

cards.name: Monster aim error and armament tiers
cards.summary: The soldier aims at the target eye and offsets the 8192 unit aim point by up to 1000 sideways and 500 vertically, then fires a blaster bolt (5 at 600), a shotgun burst (12 pellets of 2) or machine gun bursts (2).
cards.behavior: The light tier fires blaster bolts. The mid tier fires shotgun pellets. The heavy tier fires machine gun bullets. All of them aim at the enemy eye height from the muzzle, then add a uniform random offset to a point 8192 units out. The offset is up to 1000 sideways and 500 up or down. That equals about 7 degrees and 3.5 degrees. Two special shots skip the aim and fire straight ahead, so the monster can sweep a burst. The blaster bolt deals 5 and flies at 600 units per second. The shotgun burst uses the player shotgun spread and count with damage 2 and kick 1. The machine gun deals 2 damage and kick 4 per bullet, then pauses for 3 to 10 ticks of 0.1 seconds between bursts. The monster counts as headshot dead when the hit height is within 4 units of its eye, which plays a distinct death. Death below the gib health of -30 throws three meat gibs, a chest and a head.

cards.name: Gib launch velocities, lifetimes and player death
cards.summary: Gibs launch with 100 sideways and 200 to 300 up scaled by 0.7 or 1.2, clamped to 300 sideways and 200 to 500 up, live 10 to 20 seconds, and a player gibs below health -40 or respawns after 1 second.
cards.behavior: Each gib starts at a random point inside the body box. Its velocity is the dead body velocity plus a random push. The push has up to 100 in each horizontal axis and 200 plus up to 100 up. It is scaled by 0.7 when the killing hit dealt under 50 and by 1.2 otherwise. Organic gibs also halve that push. Then the velocity is clamped to 300 in each horizontal axis and to between 200 and 500 up, so every gib flies upward. Gibs spin up to 600 degrees per second and free themselves 10 to 20 seconds later. A player gibs when health falls below -40. A monster gibs at its own gib health. The player drops 4 meat gibs and a head. A normal player death keeps a corpse whose hull top is lowered to -8, tosses the weapon, clears powerups, and shows a camera tilted 40 degrees in roll and -15 in pitch toward the killer. In single player any button respawns after a 1 second delay.

constants.unit: damage points; below it the push is scaled by 0.7

cards.name: Server entity gravity, speed clamp and friction at 10 Hz
cards.summary: Non-player entities step every 0.1 second with gravity 800 applied as 80 units per second per tick, a 2000 speed clamp per axis, friction 6 with stop speed 100, and flyers using a third of the vertical friction.
cards.behavior: Projectiles, gibs, items and monsters share this tick. Each tick adds gravity times the entity gravity scale times 0.1 to the vertical speed, so a falling item gains 80 units per second per tick. Each velocity axis is clamped to 2000 first. Free movers advance by velocity times 0.1 and slide on contact. Bouncing objects reflect with a factor of 1.5. Other tossed objects slide. A tossed object that touches a floor with normal above 0.7 stops, and a bouncer stops only when its vertical speed is under 60. Walking monsters use a step mover with ground friction 6 and stop speed 100. Water friction is 1 per depth level. Flying monsters that gain vertical speed lose it at a third of the ground friction. Fast falls over a tenth of the gravity per second play a landing sound. The slide mover uses up to 4 bumps and 5 planes like player movement. Do not use these numbers for the player. The player uses the per-command step instead.

constants.name: gravity
constants.unit: units per second squared; server default, a map can override it

constants.name: step mover friction
constants.unit: dimensionless factor applied per 0.1 second tick

constants.name: step mover stop speed
constants.unit: units per second floor on the friction speed

constants.name: flyer vertical friction divisor
constants.unit: ground friction divided by this for vertical motion

constants.name: landing sound speed factor
constants.unit: fraction of gravity as downward speed that triggers the sound

cards.name: Push, hurt and gravity trigger volumes
cards.summary: A push volume sets velocity to its direction times speed times 10 (default speed 1000), a hurt volume deals 5 damage per 0.1 second tick by default, and the gravity volume does not change player gravity.
cards.behavior: A push volume replaces the velocity of a touching live body or grenade with the volume direction times its speed times 10. It does not add. The default speed is 1000 when the map gives none. For players it also copies the pushed velocity into the previous velocity record, so the landing does not hurt. A wind sound plays at most once per 1.5 seconds. A once flag removes the volume after one use. A hurt volume damages anything touching it every 0.1 second server tick, or once per second with the slow flag. The default damage is 5 per hit, which is 50 per second. The damage sound plays on every tenth frame. A flag lets the damage skip all protection. The gravity volume sets a per entity gravity scale on whatever touches it. Player movement reads only the global gravity value each command, so this source gives the player no gravity change from that volume. It affects tossed entities and monsters.

constants.name: push default speed
constants.unit: speed value before the factor of 10

constants.name: push velocity factor
constants.unit: multiplier from the speed value to units per second

constants.name: slow hurt period
constants.unit: seconds between hits with the slow flag

constants.name: hurt sound frame interval
constants.unit: server frames (10 Hz) between sound plays

cards.name: Drowning, lava and slime damage
cards.summary: Players hold their breath 12 seconds, then drown for 2 rising by 2 each second up to 15 ignoring armor, while lava deals 3 times the depth level and slime 1 times the depth level every 0.1 second tick.
cards.behavior: The air timer is set to 12 seconds ahead whenever the head is out of water. When the head is under water and the timer has passed, the drowning check runs once per second. The first hit deals 4, because the damage counter starts at 2 and adds 2 first. Each next hit adds 2 more, capped at 15. Drowning ignores armor. Lava deals 3 times the depth level each server tick, which is up to 9 per 0.1 second. The environment suit cuts this to 1 times the depth level. Slime deals 1 times the depth level per tick and the suit removes it. Both liquid damages are normal damage, so armor absorbs them. The rebreather and the environment suit refill the air timer to 10 seconds while the head is under water. A gasp sound plays on surfacing, and entering water posts a noise.

constants.name: drown damage start
constants.unit: damage points; first hit adds the step before dealing

constants.name: lava damage per depth level
constants.unit: damage points per depth level per server tick (10 Hz)

constants.name: suited lava damage per depth level
constants.unit: damage points per depth level per server tick (10 Hz)

capabilities: breath timer with ramping drown damage
